subject: PilotCorp pilot: buffer provisioning & autoscale waiver
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PilotCorp pilot: buffer provisioning & autoscale waiver

Hi Marcus / Grace (cc Kim),

PilotCorp is kicking off their staged pilot next week and we have a narrow window to make sure the Dedicated side won't throttle their end-to-end experience. High level ask: can infra provision a temporary nightly buffer for the pilot + an autoscale waiver for the defined test windows so they can burst beyond soft-limits during load tests?

Details:
- Pilot window: Aug 28–Sep 03 (internal canary Aug 28), main tests Aug 29–Sep 02
- Requested buffer: target equivalent of ~8 A100-class GPUs (they've modeled ~20% headroom over expected peak)
- Preferred nightly reservation windows: 00:00–04:00 UTC (warm caches matter)
- Autoscale waiver: allow burst to 2x soft-limit for 6h test windows; waiver should be scoped to this deal only and revert automatically

Attached: pilot_buffer_calc.xlsx (their expected concurrency/throughput), runbook_playbook.md (draft).

Questions for infra: what's the simplest path — temporary reservation vs. autoscale waiver? What telemetry/guards do we need to avoid blowouts for other customers? Cost estimate please.

Requesting answers by EOD Aug 22 so we can confirm with PilotCorp tomorrow.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
(aisha_rahman@redwood.com)

Attachments: pilot_buffer_calc.xlsx, runbook_playbook.md

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PilotCorp pilot: buffer provisioning & autoscale waiver

Thanks Aisha — quick clarifying questions before I size this out:
- Is the 8-GPU-equivalent burst continuous for the 4h window or spiky (p95 spikes)?
- Expected avg sequence length and tokens/s at peak? (affects KV cache warm-up and batching benefits)
- Do they need reserved IP/placement (hot-lanes) or just capacity headroom?

Operational note: a scoped temporary reservation is cleaner for isolation and predictable billing; an autoscale waiver is faster but risks cross-customer impact unless we gate by customer tag and strict fallback. I sketched a cost and outage-risk calc — attached capacity_estimate_v1.csv.

If they truly need warm KV cache guarantees, we'll need pre-warming tasks and a short lead time (~24h) to populate caches. Otherwise we can give a reservation window and run the canary.

I can turn this into a short runbook (ops steps + rollback) once we lock windows.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Infrastructure Lead, Serving Runtime
(marcus_lin@redwood.com)

Attachments: capacity_estimate_v1.csv

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 14:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PilotCorp pilot: buffer provisioning & autoscale waiver

Appreciate the context. A few product priorities to surface:
- PilotCorp is on an enterprise track; we should prefer predictable isolation for them (reservation) but balance with our pool utilization SLAs.
- If we do reservation, cap at 12 GPUs for nightly windows (compromise between Aisha's ask and typical utilization).
- If we go waiver route, require automatic throttles: revert to baseline after 6h and circuit-breaker at 3x baseline to avoid cost runaway.

Can we also add a fallback policy so that if other SLA-bound customers request capacity we can evict the pilot buffer gracefully (with 10m notice)? I want to avoid surprises.

Let's target a canary on Aug 28 with a runbook link: https://redwood.internal/doc/pilot-runbooks/PC-488 — we should attach the final runbook to the Deal record.

Grace O'Connor
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
(grace_oconnor@redwood.com)

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@pilotcorp.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PilotCorp pilot: buffer provisioning & autoscale waiver

Thanks Aisha — quick answers from our side:
- Confirm windows: 00:00–04:00 UTC (we can shift +-30m if needed)
- Expected peak: ~600 concurrent sessions, avg seq length 1,200 tokens, bursty p95 spikes for ~10–15m every hour
- Warm caches: yes, we get a 40% latency improvement when KV caches are warm. We'd love a warm lane if feasible.
- We're comfortable with a nightly reservation for the pilot; waiver only if reservation isn't possible.

Let us know final cost / billback model.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
SRE, PilotCorp
(liam@pilotcorp.com)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam@pilotcorp.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: PilotCorp pilot: buffer provisioning & autoscale waiver — decision summary and action items

Team — summary and next steps based on threads below: (please reply if I've mis-stated anything)

Decisions:
- Provide a nightly reservation (preferred) for the pilot: 10 GPU-equivalent capacity reserved 00:00–04:00 UTC for Aug 28–Sep 02 (compromise between ask and product concerns).
- No permanent autoscale waiver. If reservation can't be provisioned in time, grant scoped autoscale waiver for canary window only (Aug 28) with automatic revert and circuit breaker at 3x baseline.
- Add pre-warm job 30 minutes before window to populate KV cache (ops will run).

Action items:
- Marcus: finalize reservation mechanism + cost estimate and post runbook to INFRA-1124 by EOD Aug 24. (attachment: capacity_estimate_v1.csv)
- Grace: approve fallback eviction rules and confirm 10m eviction notice is acceptable to product by Aug 24.
- Kimberly: include billing note in the Deal (DC-4871) and confirm pass-through charge model to PilotCorp.
- Liam / PilotCorp: confirm you accept 10 GPU reservation (we proposed 10; you asked for 8 — we chose 10 to be conservative) by EOD Aug 23.

Links / artifacts: https://redwood.internal/doc/pilot-runbooks/PC-488, JIRA INFRA-1124 — I've attached the calculation spreadsheet and draft runbook for reference.

If nobody objects, I'll mark this as approved and schedule the canary on Aug 28 morning.

Thanks — Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
(aisha_rahman@redwood.com)
